source.author: lucr
source.text: quod si immortalis nostra foret mens, non tam se moriens dissolvi conquereretur, sed magis ire foras vestemque relinquere, ut anguis.
source.text_original: quod si immortalis nostra foret mens, / non tam se moriens dissolvi conquereretur, / sed magis ire foras vestemque relinquere, ut anguis.
source.text_english: But if our mind were immortal, dying would not complain so much that it was being dissolved, but rather that it was going out and leaving behind its garment, like a snake.

reuse.author: lact
reuse.text: quodsi immortalis nostra foret mens, non tam se moriens dissolui conquereretur, sed magis ire foras uestemque relinquere, ut anguis, equidem numquam uidi qui se quereretur in morte dissolui:
reuse.text_original: quodsi immortalis nostra foret mens, non tam se moriens dissolui conquereretur, sed magis ire foras uestemque relinquere, ut anguis, equidem numquam uidi qui se quereretur in morte dissolui:
reuse.text_english: But if our mind were immortal, it would not, when dying, complain so much that it is being dissolved, but rather that it is going out and leaving its garment, like a serpent. Indeed, I have never seen anyone who complained that he was being dissolved in death.
